text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, hoping for a deal with the PLO on implementing an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron, has cancelled a visit to the United States, his office said on Wednesday.

"That's correct," a spokeswoman in Netanyahu's office said when asked to confirm reports by Israel's Channel One and Channel Two television stations that Netanyhahu had cancelled his trip. Netanyahu was to have left late on Wednesday.
Israel and the Palestinians struggled on Wednesday to sew up a deal on Hebron in the West Bank only hours before Netanyahu's scheduled departure on a trip to the United States.
The negotiators took a break at mid-day and were to resume talks on Wednesday night.
Palestinian officials said the talks were stalemated over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to enter Palestinian-controlled parts of Hebron in "hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.

Earlier in the day, Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel said the sides had achieved "significant progress" and were trying to define how Israeli forces might operate against what he called "terrorists" in Palestinian-run areas.
